title: Bitcoin Falls Below $65,000, Lowest Since July, as Hike Bets and Liquidations Mount; MSCI Exit Weighs on Strategy
dek: Bitcoin slipped below $65,000 on Sunday, its lowest since July, as December Fed hike bets, liquidations and rotation toward AI stocks weighed. CoinGecko showed about $65,500 at our Sunday check.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: Gold-colored Bitcoin coin bearing the BTC symbol

keyPoints: Bitcoin fell below $65,000 on Sunday, its lowest since July: $64,962.10 in a LiveMint report published 10:59 a.m. IST (about 12:30 a.m. ET) Nov. 15. CoinGecko showed $65,522.31 at our Sunday check.
CoinGecko put the Bitcoin market capitalization at about $1.32 trillion; LiveMint put total crypto market capitalization at $2.19 trillion.

Drivers: a 100% CME FedWatch hike probability for Dec. 9 (CNBC, Nov. 13); a break below the roughly $73,000 200-day average (GSR via LiveMint); about $2 billion of 24-hour liquidations, mostly longs (Coinglass via LiveMint).
Rotation: DACM's Richard Galvin says the Anthropic IPO may be drawing capital from crypto, which he calls a short-term funding source for retail investors (LiveMint).
Monday: MSTR closed Friday at $111.62 and COIN touched a 52-week low of $126.90; neither has a Sunday quote in our sources. MSCI removes Strategy after the Nov. 30 close.
body:
Bitcoin fell below $72,000 on Thursday, Nov. 12, its lowest level since mid-August, as traders absorbed a hotter inflation report, higher bets on a December Federal Reserve rate hike and a sharp drop in Strategy, the largest corporate holder of the token.

## Afternoon update

At 3:57 p.m. ET Saturday, Bitcoin was quoted at $64,733.68, down about 5.3% on the day, in a Reuters market report carried by MarketScreener. Crypto Times reported $1.26 billion in 24-hour crypto liquidations and said they hit leveraged longs.

Earlier Saturday prices vary by provider and time stamp. Crypto Times, citing CoinGecko data, put Bitcoin at $67,380 at 3:17 a.m. UTC (Crypto Times, Nov. 14). TokenPost reported $66,969 at 8:02 a.m. ET (TokenPost, Nov. 14). A Yahoo Finance article put it at $66,485 on Saturday morning, down 3.96% over 24 hours and 12.26% over seven days (Yahoo Finance). CoinSpectator said Bitcoin was near $67,200, below its 200-week moving average, and down more than 10% this week (CoinSpectator, Nov. 14). Crypto Times, citing CoinGlass, reported $1.26 billion in liquidations over 24 hours, with longs making up 86.4% of the total (Crypto Times, Nov. 14). Spot bitcoin ETFs posted $284 million in net outflows on Nov. 12, a sixth straight session, per SoSoValue (Crypto Times, Nov. 14). Complete Friday flow data had not been published when that report was written. Liquidation and ETF flow totals differ by provider and cutoff time.

## The price move

Bitcoin Magazine reported that the token was near $71,800 at the time of writing on Thursday morning. Yahoo Finance's live coverage said bitcoin was down about 8% so far in November. Bitcoin.com reported that crypto derivatives liquidations topped $650 million over 24 hours, with long positions unwinding as prices slipped.

The slide follows a week in which bitcoin tracked the tech sector. It fell on Monday when the Nvidia probe weighed on markets, then lagged Wednesday's rebound in chip stocks, according to Bitcoin Magazine.

## The index exit

MSCI confirmed on Wednesday evening that Strategy will leave its USA Index as part of its November 2026 review. The removal also takes the company out of the MSCI World and ACWI indexes, effective at the Nov. 30 close. Metaplanet, the Japanese bitcoin treasury company, is slated for removal from MSCI's Japan Small Cap index on the same date (CoinReporter).

Index funds will sell Strategy shares, not bitcoin. Nothing in the index rules requires Strategy to sell its own coins. The effect is more indirect: a weaker share price makes it harder for the company to raise capital for new purchases. Strategy's CEO Phong Le pointed to $21 billion raised so far this year on the company's October earnings call, according to Yahoo Finance.

## Flows and rates

Spot bitcoin ETFs continued to see withdrawals. BlackRock's IBIT accounted for $269.7 million of Wednesday's redemptions, its ninth straight session of outflows, Bitcoin Magazine reported.

Rates matter here too. Thursday's jobless claims report did not ease the outlook for Fed policy, and CME FedWatch still shows traders pricing a quarter-point December hike. Higher rates raise the cost of holding an asset that pays no interest, which has kept pressure on bitcoin all week, Bitcoin Magazine said.

## What to watch

The October producer price index was released at 8:30 a.m. ET Friday, at +0.3% against a 0.4% forecast (BLS; CNBC). Investors will also watch whether bitcoin holds the $70,000 area that analysts cited as the next support level, and whether the MSCI effective date on Nov. 30 brings forced selling in Strategy shares.

This is market analysis. The figures above come from the cited outlets and are not a forecast of future prices.

## Late-session print

By 3:59 p.m. ET, MarketAlleys showed bitcoin at $71,415, down 4.32% over 24 hours. That is one secondary aggregator; other Thursday quotes ran from about $72,700 to $73,500 earlier in the session (Yahoo Finance; Substack). The MSCI removal of Strategy takes effect after the close on Nov. 30 (Yahoo Finance).

## Friday update

Bitcoin fell below $70,000 early Friday, Nov. 13, for the first time since August, and traded near $68,600 at 11:59 a.m. ET, down more than 4% over 24 hours (Investopedia, citing CoinDesk). Strategy shares were down nearly 5% at the same time (Investopedia).

## Sunday update

Bitcoin fell below $65,000 on Sunday, its lowest level since July. LiveMint put it at $64,962.10 in a report published at 10:59 a.m. IST (about 12:30 a.m. ET) on Nov. 15. When we checked CoinGecko on Sunday (the page does not show its capture time), it showed $65,522.31 and a Bitcoin market capitalization of about $1.32 trillion. LiveMint put the total crypto market capitalization at $2.19 trillion. LiveMint's quote carries only its publication time, and the CoinGecko figures are a snapshot from our check, so treat both as readings rather than a live price.

### What is pushing it down

- **Rates.** CME FedWatch odds for the Dec. 9 meeting stood at 100% for a hike on Friday, with about 89% for a quarter-point and 14% for a half-point (CNBC, Nov. 13). The 10-year Treasury yield was 5.143% in Friday trading (CNBC). Higher yields make non-yielding assets such as Bitcoin harder to hold.
- **Technicals and liquidations.** GSR told LiveMint the move may be technical, saying Bitcoin "broke down through its 200-day moving average of about $73,000, which has caused a slew of liquidations and new shorts to develop." Coinglass tracked about $2 billion of crypto liquidations in the 24 hours through 9 a.m. Sunday in Singapore, including $774 million in Bitcoin and $488 million in Ether. Most of it hit long positions (LiveMint).
- **Rotation.** Richard Galvin of DACM told LiveMint the Anthropic IPO "may be drawing capital away from crypto," and that crypto "remains a short-term funding source, particularly for retail investors." The Anthropic IPO is reported for Nov. 19.

### Monday read-through for MSTR and COIN

- **MSTR.** Strategy closed Friday at $111.62, down 2.4% (MarketBeat, Nov. 13). Our sources have no Sunday or Monday quote for it. The MSCI removal takes effect after the Nov. 30 close, and index funds may sell before then.
- **COIN.** Coinbase touched a 52-week low of $126.90 on Friday, against a prior close of $130.67 (MarketBeat, Nov. 13). We have no Sunday quote. Our view is that a further Bitcoin decline would add pressure on COIN at Monday's open, which is the first test.
- **Dated checkpoints.** Nov. 18 FOMC minutes, and the Nov. 30 MSCI effective date.

marketImpact.summary: The slide has three sources: a December Fed hike that markets now treat as close to certain, forced selling after the break of the 200-day average, and capital rotating toward the Anthropic IPO. The dated overhang for Strategy remains the MSCI removal after the Nov. 30 close.
